exposure: night-eating (>50% of total energy intake from 1900 to 0659 h)
short sleep duration (<6 h night sleep)
cohort: 673 pregnant women from the Growing Up in Singapore Towards healthy Outcomes (GUSTO) cohort.
finding: Night-eating was associated with a 0.45 weeks shortening of gestation length and 2.19-fold higher odds of delivering preterm, while short sleep was associated with a 0.33 weeks shortening of gestation length.
